text: This is the law of the guilt offering; it is most holy.
The guilt offering shall be slaughtered in the place where the burnt offering is slaughtered, and its blood shall be thrown against the altar on every side.
All its fat shall be offered: the fat tail, the fat that covers the entrails,
the two kidneys with the fat on them at the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which he shall remove along with the kidneys.
The priest shall burn them on the altar as a food offering to the LORD; it is a guilt offering.
Every male among the priests may eat of it. It shall be eaten in a holy place; it is most holy.
The guilt offering is like the sin offering; there is one law for them both. It belongs to the priest who makes atonement with it.
And the priest who offers anyone's burnt offering shall keep for himself the hide of the burnt offering he has offered.
Every grain offering baked in an oven, and everything prepared in a pan or on a griddle, belongs to the priest who offers it.
But every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron alike, each one the same as his brother.
This is the law of the fellowship offering that one may present to the LORD.

If he offers it as a thank offering, then along with the thank offering he shall present unleavened loaves mixed with oil, unleavened wafers spread with oil, and loaves of fine flour well kneaded and mixed with oil.
Along with loaves of leavened bread he shall present his offering, together with his thanksgiving fellowship offering.

versions.text: With his thanksgiving fellowship offering he shall present his offering with loaves of leavened bread.
versions.explanation: The doubled "with ... with" construction is awkward for oral reading, and the current word order obscures the Hebrew sequence, which begins with the leavened loaves. Reordering follows the Hebrew and reads more smoothly aloud.

text: From each kind of offering he shall present one loaf as a contribution to the LORD; it belongs to the priest who throws the blood of the fellowship offering.

versions.text: From each offering he shall present one of every kind as a contribution to the LORD; it belongs to the priest who throws the blood of the fellowship offering.
versions.explanation: "From each offering ... one of every kind" is redundant and unclear. The Hebrew means one item (loaf) is taken from each kind of bread offering; the revision states this plainly and reads better aloud.

text: The meat of his thanksgiving fellowship offering shall be eaten on the day it is offered; none of it may be left until morning.
But if his offering is a vow or a freewill offering, it shall be eaten on the day he presents his sacrifice, and what is left over may be eaten the next day.
Whatever remains of the meat of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned up.

If any of the meat of his fellowship offering is eaten on the third day, it will not be accepted. It will not be credited to the one who offered it; it is tainted, and the person who eats of it will bear his guilt.
Meat that touches anything unclean must not be eaten; it shall be burned up. As for other meat, anyone who is clean may eat it.
But the person who eats meat from the LORD's fellowship offering while unclean shall be cut off from his people.

And if anyone touches something unclean—human uncleanness, an unclean animal, or any unclean, detestable creature—and then eats the meat of the LORD's fellowship offering, that person shall be cut off from his people.
The LORD said to Moses:
Say to the Israelites: You shall not eat any fat of an ox, a sheep, or a goat.
The fat of an animal found dead or torn by wild beasts may be used for any other purpose, but you must not eat it.
For anyone who eats the fat of an animal from which a food offering is presented to the LORD shall be cut off from his people.
Wherever you live, you must not eat the blood of any bird or animal.
Anyone who eats blood shall be cut off from his people.
The LORD said to Moses:
Say to the Israelites: Whoever offers a fellowship offering to the LORD shall bring part of it as his gift to the LORD.
With his own hands he shall bring the food offerings of the LORD; he shall bring the fat together with the breast, so that the breast may be waved as a wave offering before the LORD.
The priest shall burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.
You shall give the right thigh to the priest as a contribution from your fellowship offerings.
The son of Aaron who offers the blood and the fat of the fellowship offering shall have the right thigh as his portion.

For I have taken the breast of the wave offering and the thigh of the contribution from the Israelites, from their fellowship offerings, and I have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as a perpetual due from the Israelites.
This is the portion of Aaron and the portion of his sons from the food offerings of the LORD, assigned to them on the day they were presented to serve the LORD as priests.
On the day they were anointed, the LORD commanded that this be given them by the Israelites. It is a perpetual statute throughout their generations.
This is the law of the burnt offering, the grain offering, the sin offering, the guilt offering, the ordination offering, and the fellowship offering,
which the LORD commanded Moses on Mount Sinai on the day he commanded the Israelites to present their offerings to the LORD in the Wilderness of Sinai.
